clue.text: MP: I am undone, ruined — all hell breaking loose!

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the preceding words are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician despairs that they are finished as chaos erupts around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' tells you to rearrange MP, I, AM and UNDONE, eleven letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Total uproar and chaos is the sense; Milton's capital of Hell gave us the word.

clue.text: Hanger-on in a place where soldiers train?

parts.note: paras are paratroopers, a common crossword shorthand for soldiers
a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: Someone lingering about an army training ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: a PARA SITE would be a place where paratroopers train.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger who lives off others is a figurative leech, a hanger-on.

clue.text: Bird from north once visible to all on roof?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone
a thatch is a roof of straw or reeds

explanation.surface: A northern bird once seen perched on a rooftop.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating meaning anyone may watch; 'on' places N and U above THATCH in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A small woodland songbird that climbs tree trunks, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Duck finds fish in English river

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, the fish placed within the outer letters

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe

explanation.surface: A duck spots a fish swimming in an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sea duck prized for its soft down, so an example of a duck.

clue.text: Unity makes no sense when there's confusion

indicators.note: confusion here means the letters of the preceding words are jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a notion of togetherness becomes meaningless amid muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when there's confusion' says rearrange NO and SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one whole and undivided is the meaning, a synonym for unity.

clue.text: I would start to embrace friend if possible

parts.note: the contraction I'd stands for I would

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here of embrace

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone saying they would begin to hug a friend, given the chance.
explanation.definitionFit: In the best circumstances, as one would wish, so a synonym for if possible.

clue.text: Serve out soup, meat -around end of dinner, cheese

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece
serving out spreads the food around, so the letters of the next two words are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of dinner

explanation.surface: Instructions for dishing up a meal: soup, then meat, then cheese to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve out' is the anagram signal and 'around' the container. In Britain the answer is slang for cheap, ordinary cheese, the sort used to bait traps.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for low-grade hard cheese, the kind fit for baiting a trap.

clue.text: Fantastic beer belly? Pounds must be lost

indicators.note: losing something means taking it out, so the pounds letter is removed

parts.note: flab is the fat that makes a beer belly
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A drinker is told that shedding weight would make a fine beer gut look fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for pounds (as in the £ sign, from libra).
explanation.definitionFit: Slang of the sixties for wonderful or great, a synonym for fantastic.

clue.text: Activity in Edinburgh or one of the Borders?

definitions.meaning: the Edinburgh Festival ... is the huge arts festival running alongside the official one
an edge or border; the Borders is also the Scottish region near Edinburgh

explanation.surface: Something going on in the Scottish capital or down in the Border country.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh's alternative arts festival, and an edge or margin of something.

clue.text: Dictionary man will certainly dispatch a few pints

definitions.meaning: Ebenezer Cobham ... compiled ... Dictionary of Phrase and Fable

definitions.text: will certainly dispatch a few pints
definitions.meaning: a beer maker sends out a good deal of ale

explanation.surface: A lexicographer who would happily see off several pints.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian compiler of a famous reference book, and a maker of beer.

clue.text: Unfaithful lover, English duke highly regarded

parts.note: a rat is a disloyal person who betrays a partner

explanation.surface: A two-timing English aristocrat who is nonetheless much admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed or ranked highly, so a past participle matching highly regarded.

clue.text: Devon's water reduced — I have to get after that board

parts.note: the Exe is a river flowing through Devon to Exeter
cut means reduced or lowered
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A complaint that the Devon water supply has been cut, so the speaker must chase the company directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is the river of Devon in south-west England; 'after that' just puts I'VE after the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior managers of a company collectively, i.e. its governing board.

clue.text: A gap through the flight path

definitions.text: A gap through the flight path

parts.words: A gap through the flight path
parts.note: not an aircraft route: the flight is a flight of stairs, and this is the vertical shaft they wind around

explanation.surface: A break in the route planes follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical opening inside a building in which a staircase rises.

clue.text: Bore keen to be heard

indicators.note: something heard is spoken, so the word for keen is taken by its sound

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: A tedious person anxious to get a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it is a tidal wave surging up a river; EAGRE is an old word for one, as on the River Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal surge running up an estuary, the second sense of the word bore.

clue.text: Teachers with red pens, say, making hearts

definitions.meaning: people who mark right answers with a tick
ticker is slang for the heart, which ticks like a clock

explanation.surface: Teachers wielding red pens bring delight to their pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Markers who tick work, and informal slang for the heart.

clue.text: Cheer overthrow of government endlessly with anger all around

indicators.note: the anger word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to enrage is to anger

indicators.note: endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: a coup is the sudden overthrow of a government

explanation.surface: Rebels cheer the fall of the regime amid widespread fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheer' looks like a noun of applause but is the verb. 'endlessly' trims the coup word's last letter; 'all around' puts the anger word round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone on is to urge and hearten them, a synonym verb.

clue.text: Bowl from city going back to Roman times()

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to ... a batsman is to bowl them out with a yorker, a ball pitching at their feet

definitions.text: city going back to Roman times
definitions.meaning: the northern English city was the Roman Eboracum

explanation.surface: A dish from an ancient city with Roman roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like a dish, but it is the cricket verb. A yorker is a ball aimed at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket verb for dismissing with a full-length ball, and a cathedral city founded by Romans.

clue.text: Someone publicising a new book? One may get a rocket

definitions.meaning: a person who holds a book launch
a device that fires a rocket or missile

explanation.surface: A publicist promoting a title who risks a severe telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get a rocket' suggests a British telling-off; here it is a firing device holding a missile.
explanation.definitionFit: One who introduces a product to market, and a device that fires missiles.

clue.text: Where a tramp may rest incidentally

definitions.meaning: a vagrant sleeps at the roadside
a phrase introducing a passing remark

explanation.surface: A tramp's resting place, mentioned in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally at the roadside, and idiomatically meaning in passing.

clue.text: Glance through only half the sordid stories?

indicators.note: keeping only half means dropping the back four letters of the eight

parts.note: scandals are shocking or disgraceful stories

explanation.surface: Skimming just some of the tabloid gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps the first four letters of SCANDALS.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over quickly is to skim, a synonym verb phrase.

clue.text: A room in back parts of plane? Not that part of plane

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
the back of a word is its end, so its final letters are taken

parts.note: a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: A cabin in the rear of an aircraft, though not that bit of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back parts of' takes the last two letters of the first 'plane'. 'Not that part of plane' warns that the second 'plane' means an aircraft, not the written word.
explanation.definitionFit: The streamlined housing for an aircraft engine, a component of the aeroplane.

clue.text: Art on the box?

parts.note: not television: box is the shrub, clipped into decorative shapes

explanation.surface: Culture as broadcast on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental clipping of hedges such as box into shapes, a garden art.

clue.text: Communicate with maiden leaving shipment

indicators.note: the maiden letter departs from the word for communicate

parts.note: to transmit is to communicate or send a message
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with a girl who is departing on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: M for maiden comes from cricket scorecards, where a maiden is an over with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage of goods from place to place, i.e. conveyance or shipment.

clue.text: Double bend -and one sort of driver may be despicable

parts.note: the letter S has the shape of a double bend, as on road signs
a cabby drives a taxi

explanation.surface: A road with an S-bend where a careless driver behaves badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally meaning contemptible or mean, as well as covered in scabs.

clue.text: Young bird or seal being heard

indicators.note: something heard is spoken aloud, so the seal word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: A fledgling or a seal pup barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' looks like the animal, but it is a stamp for wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile swan, so a specific young bird.

clue.text: Animal retiring by set having lost tail

parts.note: coy means shy or retiring

indicators.note: losing the tail means the last letter goes

parts.note: to put something is to set it down

explanation.surface: A shy creature beside a tail-less group.
explanation.definitionFit: A large South American rodent, also called nutria, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Bird responsible for muck in church

parts.note: chaff is husks and worthless rubbish

explanation.surface: A bird blamed for the mess left inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but here it just supplies its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European finch with a pink breast, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Things that may be poisonous? Enjoyable and good, I found

parts.note: fun means enjoyable, as in a fun day

explanation.surface: A forager warned about toxic mushrooms but finding them fun all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms and toadstools include many toxic species, so things that may be poisonous.

clue.text: Naval equipment thrown into Len's cabin

indicators.note: thrown means put into disarray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive gives the letters of Len plus S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ship's gear tossed into a sailor's cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' scrambles LENS and CABIN; here the apostrophe's S does count as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Housings on a ship's deck holding the compass, items of naval equipment.

clue.text: Expertise coming through to the audience? Not at all

indicators.note: what reaches an audience is what they hear, so the expertise word is taken by sound

parts.note: know-how means practical expertise

explanation.surface: A performer's skill reaching the audience fails completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect or informal for in no way, a synonym for not at all.

clue.text: You may need a little time to finish still

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A reassurance that a bit more time is needed to complete the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish' just puts T at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to now, so far; in that sense yet and still are synonyms.

clue.text: Ionised emission from torpedo?

definitions.meaning: a charged beam given off, read literally as electric plus ray
the torpedo is a fish that stuns prey with an electric shock

explanation.surface: Charged radiation emitted from a weapon fired by a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torpedo' looks like a naval weapon, but it is also the name of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish that delivers electric shocks, also called torpedo; literally a charged beam.
